target_customer: Non-technical users, freelancers, agencies and ops teams who automate workflows; originally NYC building owners and contractors seeking energy-efficiency subsidies
problem: Automating manual work normally requires coding or complex tools. RetroFix lets users describe a workflow in plain English and an agent builds and monitors it. Earlier the team targeted the paperwork for building energy rebates.
business_model: SaaS subscription for workflow automation (early access); earlier concept was a service for rebate applications

founders.name: Isaac Toscano
founders.background_notes: Built financial models for billion-dollar companies (employers not named) and did solar cell research at MIT Nano lab per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building an agent that writes workflows and code against 2,000+ app APIs on top of LLMs was standard engineering with reliability challenges in 2024.

defensibility.rationale: Zapier and many AI-native entrants offer similar natural language builders; the integrations library is commodity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zapier shipped natural language orchestration (Zapier Central) per search results; no acquisition of RetroFix found.

market_need_then: Demand for automation was proven by large incumbents like Zapier, and LLMs made natural language workflow creation newly possible in 2024. For the original rebate idea, YC launch copy pitched it as a TurboTax for building rebates.

branding.domain_note: retrofix.ai; a separate unrelated photo restoration app is also called RetroFix.

identity.visual_style: Plain software landing page marked Now in Early Access
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, plain-language headlines about automations that actually work

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community found about the brand; name collides with other RetroFix products and fit the earlier retrofit idea more than workflow automation.

pivots.from: Applying for government energy-efficiency subsidies and rebates for NYC buildings (YC launch post, July 2024)

outcome_analysis: RetroFix launched in summer 2024 as a rebate paperwork tool, then repositioned to plain English workflow automation in a crowded category led by Zapier. It remains in early access with two MIT founders and no verifiable funding beyond YC. Outcome is undetermined; a thin moat and heavy competition are the main risks.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, Startups.fm) list 500K pre-seed from YC; unverified, no round recorded. The competitor search returned only 2025 to 2026 pages, nothing dated near the batch, so the list is left empty. Location conflicts between San Francisco and New York in sources. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed dated 2024-09 rests on VCBacked alone, a single database.
